_note: Curated, hand-written (not auto-fetched) summaries of genuinely new AI agent capabilities, verified against real sources before writing — see each entry's tryIt links for the primary source.

capabilities.title: Computer & Browser Use Agents
capabilities.tagline: AI that operates a computer for you, not just gives advice
capabilities.whatItIs: Instead of only answering questions or drafting text, these agents directly control a computer or browser — looking at the screen, moving a cursor, clicking buttons, and typing — to complete multi-step tasks on their own. OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra (released September 2026) is built specifically around this, and Anthropic's Claude has a dedicated "computer use" tool with the same idea.
capabilities.howItWorks: The model is given a screenshot of the current screen and a toolset (click, type, scroll, screenshot, etc.). It decides which action to take, the environment executes it and returns a new screenshot, and the loop repeats until the task is done or it needs your input — no custom API integration with the target app required.
pros: Automates real GUI work — filling out forms, running frontend QA checks, data entry — in apps that have no API
Handles multi-step tasks (research, then draft, then submit) without you scripting each step
cons: Anthropic explicitly warns against using it for tasks needing perfect precision or sensitive data without human review
Mis-clicks and misreads of the screen still happen — it needs to be watched, not left fully unattended

capabilities.title: Persistent Memory Across Sessions
capabilities.tagline: Assistants that remember you instead of starting from zero every time
capabilities.whatItIs: AI assistants now carry facts, preferences, and context forward between separate conversations, instead of forgetting everything the moment a chat ends. Anthropic rolled persistent memory out to all Claude users (including free) in March 2026; ChatGPT has had memory since 2024 and added a background-curation feature called "Dreaming" in June 2026.
capabilities.howItWorks: Claude periodically extracts structured "memory objects" — stated preferences, important context, notable decisions — from a conversation and stores them, transparently and editably, for future sessions to reference. ChatGPT instead synthesizes memory automatically in the background without you saving anything.
pros: No more re-explaining your role, preferences, or an ongoing project every single conversation
Claude's version is fully visible and editable — you can see and delete exactly what it stored
cons: Raises real data-retention and privacy questions — what's remembered, for how long, and who can see it
ChatGPT's automatic background synthesis is less visible and harder to audit than Claude's explicit memory objects

capabilities.title: Multi-Agent Orchestration ("Swarms")
capabilities.tagline: Many specialized agents working in parallel instead of one model doing it all
capabilities.whatItIs: Rather than one model handling a task start to finish, a swarm splits the work across multiple agent instances that run in parallel or hand off to each other. OpenAI open-sourced an early, lightweight version of this called Swarm in 2024 (since archived in favor of the fuller OpenAI Agents SDK); Anthropic's Claude Code now ships "Dynamic Workflows," where Claude writes its own orchestration script and spawns dozens to hundreds of parallel subagents in a single session.
capabilities.howItWorks: In Claude Code, Claude decomposes a goal, writes a small script that fans work out to independent subagents (each with its own context and tool permissions), runs a verification pass on their output, and reconciles the results — with progress surviving a restart. OpenAI's Swarm used a simpler model of stateless agents passing an explicit "handoff" to one another.
pros: Parallelizes large or multi-part jobs — e.g. checking many files or running many tests at once — instead of doing them one at a time
Specialized subagents can be more reliable at a narrow task than one generalist model juggling everything
cons: More moving parts means more places for something to go wrong, and more to review
Cost scales with the number of agents spawned — a large swarm is not free just because each call is small

capabilities.title: Ready-Made Business Agents
capabilities.tagline: Off-the-shelf agents instead of building your own from scratch
capabilities.whatItIs: Companies are increasingly deploying pre-built, purpose-specific agents rather than custom-building one in-house. Salesforce's Agentforce is the clearest example — it ships named, ready-to-configure agents for specific jobs (sales, service, IT/HR, supply chain) that plug directly into a company's existing data.
capabilities.howItWorks: Agentforce provides templates — Service Agent, Employee Agent, Campaign Agent, Sales Development Rep, Sales Coach, Guided Shopping, Setup Agent — plus an "AgentExchange" marketplace with 100+ prebuilt actions and templates from partners like AWS, Box, Cisco, Google Cloud, and Stripe, so a company configures rather than builds an agent.
pros: Far faster time-to-deploy than building and testing a custom agent from scratch
Comes pre-integrated with the company's existing CRM/business data
cons: Less flexible than a purpose-built custom agent — you work within the vendor's templates
Locks you into that vendor's platform and pricing model

capabilities.title: Stronger Safety Controls
capabilities.tagline: Real-time filters trained to catch jailbreaks before they work
capabilities.whatItIs: As agents get more capable and more autonomous, labs are shipping dedicated safety layers around the model itself. Anthropic's "Constitutional Classifiers" are one concrete example — input/output filters trained specifically to catch and block jailbreak attempts in real time.
capabilities.howItWorks: The classifiers are trained against a written set of principles (a "constitution") to recognize and block harmful requests and outputs, screening both what goes into the model and what comes out — without a human having to hand-write a rule for every possible attack.
pros: Measurably cuts down successful jailbreaks against frontier models compared to having no classifier layer
Doesn't require retraining the underlying model itself to add or update protections
cons: Not a solved problem: published research on "refuse-then-comply" attacks reports real success rates against current defenses (72% against Claude Haiku, 57% against GPT-4o, in controlled testing)
Adds an extra filtering step that can occasionally flag legitimate requests

capabilities.title: The September 2026 Model Wave
capabilities.tagline: Three major labs shipped new flagship models in the same week
capabilities.whatItIs: Anthropic, OpenAI, and Google all released new flagship models within days of each other in early September 2026: Anthropic's Claude Fable 5.1 and Mythos 5.1 (September 1), Google's Gemini 3.8 Flash (September 2), and OpenAI's GPT-6 Astra (September 3) — OpenAI's most capable model yet, built around computer and browser use.
capabilities.howItWorks: Each lab ships on its own release cycle, but competitive pressure compresses the gaps between major releases — when one lab ships a step-change model, others tend to follow within the same window rather than waiting for a scheduled release date.
pros: Rapid, broad improvement — whichever model you use, it's likely to keep getting meaningfully better on a short cycle
Competition between labs pushes price and performance in your favor as a user
cons: A fast-moving target if you're building on these models — one release in this wave shipped with breaking API changes
Hard to keep a stable, tested integration when the underlying model changes every few weeks
